shared_dependency_review.finding: The recorded formal conclusion starts at e1 although its premise includes e0; prose/library examples preserve the full append. Current ArrayValue(x+y) already implements that independently supported ordinary behavior. Changing it to discard a head would break normal users. No product patch follows from the printed conflict; retain A0 without making it a gate on unrelated Boolean/integer predicates.

Fixed modulo prose provides standard-mathematics wording, not a signed-remainder equation. Current remainder alone does not prove a uniquely prescribed negative-domain defect. Fractional parity has an explicit documentation integral-part versus source round conflict. Do not replace either algorithm by inference or reopen arbitrary precision. Small exact integers have a useful common parity domain despite these separate boundaries.

shared_dependency_review.point: Boolean native admission versus general source equality
shared_dependency_review.finding: Documentation describes Boolean inputs while source uses general equality. Native Boolean checks differ mechanically on other domains, but that does not settle public nonboolean admission. The complete Boolean truth tables, required x/y bindings and sole-error demand are common and independently decidable. No broad equality rewrite is proposed.
